<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
Note that the usage of letters $S$ and $\mathcal S$ for the space-time formulation and its mixed variant is not coincidental. 
    As a matter of fact, the \emph{action} integral of Hamilton's principle is, from a mechanics point of view, a natural starting point for developing a space-time form.
    For the sake of brevity, however, we refer to Schuß et al.~\cite{Schuss2023} for a discussion.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
The space-time lifting~\eqref{eq:space_time_lifting} combines spatial and temporal quantities, which have different physical dimensions.
    For dimensional consistency, the temporal coordinate could be scaled by a constant, cf.~\cite{Hesch2026}.
    It can be shown, that such a scaling factor cancels out in the final equation for the Jacobian~\eqref{eq:kinematic_jacobian} and the directional derivatives~\eqref{eq:derivative_field_function}. 
    For simplicity of presentation, such a scaling is omitted here.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
